elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall ..." — the trigger covers both expiry and any termination, and each limb ((a) assistance, (b) return, (c) deletion) hangs off that same trigger rather than off an anticipated-expiry request.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "at Client's request, provide transition assistance for up to six (6) months following such expiry or termination". The request condition is post-hoc and tied to the same expiry/termination trigger, not to anticipated expiry only.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination, return to Client all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Client" — the 30-day clock runs from termination/expiry, not from a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "... in a standard machine-readable format."

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "after such return, delete all such data from its systems and certify such deletion to Client in writing" — deletion and certification are expressly sequenced after return, so no walk-away immediate-deletion risk.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same trigger language: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Six (6) months of assistance in limb (a) exceeds the 90-day fallback floor; the excess is justified because the proposal is pitched at the preferred level.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return of all Client data within 30 days after expiry or termination in a machine-readable format, which satisfies the export requirement.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all six preferred elements appear in operative language in the inserted clause, with no reliance on the margin comment.

Data scope is correctly drawn. The agreement has no defined "Customer Data" term, and the insertion uses "all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Client", which captures every category rather than selected named data types.

Minimal: the redline is a single concise insertion for a missing clause; Sections 13, 14 and 24 are left verbatim, including the Client-favourable retention of domain and Client Content ownership and the 30/60-day name-server and hosting-environment provisions. No survival tail, at-own-expense language, procedures or other model-language extras were added beyond what the six elements require.

Preserves intent: nothing in the retained text contradicts the new clause. Section 14's run-off (services continue to the last day of the month following notice) and Section 13's Client-side migration responsibilities sit alongside, not against, a TrueLink transition and return obligation; no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created.

Drafting nit to tidy (not an element or intent failure): the inserted paragraph is unnumbered while Section 24 lists surviving provisions by number ("Sections 1 and 5 through 30"). Number it (e.g. as a new Section 15 with consequential renumbering, or as Section 14a) or add it to the Section 24 survival list so the post-termination obligations are unambiguously within the survival set.
